name: trinity-desktop
//: Exists only to carry tags; every target is still inferred from the plugins (`lint` from @nx/eslint, `test` from vitest.config.mts), so this file declares none and adding one upstream needs no edit here. Before it, `trinity-desktop` was the one Nx project with NO tags — it matched no `depConstraints` entry, so it appeared as a hole in a boundary the rest of the workspace calls closed. Measured rather than assumed: the hole is not reachable. The shell is isolated by construction — its own `tsconfig.json` (no `extends`, no `@trinity/*` paths) and its own dependency tree via `pnpm electron:install` — so neither a vendor import nor a `@trinity/*` import RESOLVES here, and `@nx/enforce-module-boundaries` needs a resolved graph node to say anything. Verified by piping both import shapes through eslint against `electron/src/main.ts`: no boundary error either way, before or after these tags. So the tags state intent and make the tagging invariant able to cover every project uniformly, rather than switching enforcement on. They also mean that if the shell ever gains the path aliases, `type:app` (the four vendor bans, as apps/trinity) and `scope:shared` (out of the matrix domain libs) already apply without a fresh decision.
